approach:
Add one reading check, `check_part_coverage(reading, request)`, as one new `step!(check_part_coverage(reading, request));` line placed last in `refusing_check` (checks.rs:546, after check_reading_references). Last position means no existing refusing case changes its first refuser. `is_bullet` and `request_text_acceptance` (topics.rs:266-282) stay untouched. A new parser `request_parts` in topics.rs reads:
(a) numbered parts, as runs 1,2,3.. of at least two members, in the forms `(N)` (line start or inline), `N.` and `N)` (line start);
(b) dash or star bullets. An `Acceptance` section is opened by a line equal (trimmed, any case, optional trailing colon) to `Acceptance`, `Acceptance:` or `Acceptance criteria`, or by a `#` heading whose text starts with Acceptance. That is the plain label line StewardRequest::new writes (steward.rs:581). The section ends at the next `#` heading or a label line such as `Files: ...` (steward.rs:585). When no such opener exists, all dash and star bullets are read.
It skips fenced blocks, `>` lines, quoted or backticked spans (`without_quoted_spans`, terms.rs:86), generator-written lines (`is_generated_line`, terms.rs:62) and everything after `## Source` in an approval request (the anchors of `plain_request_prose`, terms.rs:189-208).

DISTINCTIVE STEM (fixes finding 5). The order is fixed and written in a code comment. Tokenise into runs of letters or digits, lowercase. If longer than 4 chars and ending in `s`, drop the `s` (the singular form). Reject if shorter than 4. Reject if the raw token or the singular form is in the const stop list. The stop list holds full words, so the stop check runs BEFORE the cut to 5 chars; the entries are test, tests, pass, passes, change, changes, described, existing, job, part, request, fmt and similar. Then cut to 5 chars. A unit test pins: 'changes', 'described', 'existing', 'tests', 'pass' not distinctive; 'clippy', 'Parts'-vs-'part' handling and 'defaults'/'default' equal.

COVERAGE USES ONLY AN ITEM'S OWN STEMS (fixes finding 2). For each item (part or bullet), take its distinctive stems and remove any stem that also occurs in another item of the same request. These are its own stems. If none remain, fall back to all of its stems. If it has no stems at all (`Yes`, `No`), it is not checked. An item is covered when one criterion shares at least min(2, ceil(n/2)) of its own stems, n being the count of own stems. Part 3 'Cover the flag with a test' loses `flag` to part 1, keeps `cover`, needs one shared stem, and a criterion for parts 1 or 2 no longer covers it. The cap of 2 still lets a long-title Steward bullet `The change is made as described: <title>` pass when the criterion restates a few title words. `fmt, clippy and test pass` has only `clipp`, so dropping its criterion is refused.

DEFERRAL (fixes finding 4). Searched in summary, assumptions, departures and out_of_scope; never in criteria, because a criterion may describe the gate.
- Clause rule: sentences are split into clauses on `;` and `,`.
- Deferral phrase: a clause counts when it has a deferral phrase (follow-up, deferred, later job, separate job, not in this job, left for) and no negation guard (never, without, refus, unless, do not, not defer).
- Naming the item: the clause names the item by marker (`(3)`, `part 3`) or by the required own-stem overlap.
- Past or retry guard, applied to summary, assumptions and departures: a clause is skipped when it has earlier, previous, previously, prior, last, was, were, had, already, or a job id (`\d{8}-\d{6}-[a-z0-9]{4}`). A retry reading that recounts an earlier split is therefore not refused for it.
- out_of_scope: an item naming a marker counts without a phrase and without the past guard (a covered item listed as out of scope is a contradiction).

An item is refused when deferred or uncovered, unless the request permits a split.

SPLIT EXEMPTION (fixes findings 3 and 9). It reads only plain request sentences (not quoted, fenced or generated). Each sentence is cut into clauses on `;` and `,`, and the guards run per clause. A clause permits a split only when ALL hold:
- it has a modal (may, can, could, might, is allowed to);
- it has no negation (not, never, cannot, n't, no);
- it has none of the complaint words (earlier, previous, last, rejected, wrong, said, reading, attempt, bug);
- it has one of two shapes. Shape A is a move verb (split, move, defer, leave, handle, ship, land, deliver, do) followed by at most 4 object words, then in, into, as, to or for, an optional determiner, an optional adjective (separate, follow-up, later, next, smaller, several, multiple) and a noun from {job(s), change(s), PR(s), pull request(s), request(s)}. Object words may not contain a path- or identifier-like token (a `.`, `/` or `::`), so 'split checks.rs into separate jobs' and 'split checks.rs into modules' do not match. Shape B is a marker or part word (`(3)`, `part 3`, `item N`, `the rest`) as subject of be or become, then an optional article, then follow-up, separate or later, then job, change or PR.
A bare '<adjective> <noun>' with a modal never permits: 'A wrong count could block the next job.', 'This can stall multiple jobs.' and 'The fix might need a smaller change.' are negatives.
A permitting clause that names markers exempts only those parts. One that names none exempts every item. Under-exempting comma lists such as 'Parts (1), (2) may be...' is the safe direction and is accepted.

FIXTURES THAT THIS CHANGE BREAKS. The fake reader (fake.rs:311) emits one fixed criterion, and the CLI Scenario reader (athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs:572-573) returns a fixed `default_reading()` whatever the request says. CLI tests that queue bullet requests (drain.rs:3988, 4067, 4069, 4492, 4681, 6320; job_plan.rs:166, 169) carry bullets such as 'the demo study has a pin' that the fixed reading ('README.md ends with a greeting line', 'the tests still pass') cannot cover, so the production gate (reading.rs:722) would now refuse them.
- fake.rs: the fake reader adds one content criterion per request line that is a bullet or numbered part, with the marker stripped (`- `, `* `, `N. `, `N) `, `(N) `) and capped at 300 chars. It strips the marker so the copied criterion does not trip check_scope_limit or the producer and verifier fakes that split criteria on '. ' (finding 8).
- common/mod.rs: `Scenario::script`'s Reader branch appends the same marker-stripped lines as content criteria, next to `naming_earlier_jobs`. This file is test support and is not a listed deliverable (finding 1). It cannot be avoided: with uncovered-item refusal (required by criteria 3 and 4 and by finding 2), criterion 8 cannot hold otherwise. Editing each of the many CLI tests instead would touch more non-deliverable files, so the one-seam fix is the smallest. The plan names it plainly in `files` and `open_questions`.
- Finding 8 test: the agent crate cannot reach core, so the end-to-end proof sits in core. A corpus test calls `athena_agent::fake::deterministic_turn` with a reader invocation whose request holds two bullets and parts (1)(2)(3), parses the output into a Reading and runs `refusing_check`. It expects Accept. A fake.rs unit test pins the stripped criteria text.

The producer then runs the full `cargo test --locked` and fixes any other fixed-reading fixture at its seam, never by weakening the check.

The reader brief gets no new rule: briefs.rs and briefs/reader.rs stay unchanged (the rule section was measured at 3045 of 3150 bytes with 11 rules, briefs.rs:3555-3558). The refusal message carries the repair text.

THE 5% ESTIMATE (finding 7). The doc comment says 'expected 5% of newly refused readings' and labels it an unmeasured estimate. It states that the corpus Accept cases are built to pass and so are not a measure. It states that the replay hold limit is the declared share plus REPLAY_DECLARED_MARGIN_POINTS = 5 points (replay.rs:161, 304-307), so 5 declared gives a hold at over 10%. It says the replay at verification is where the figure is measured. If the producer's loop runs a replay and reports a newly refused share, that figure replaces the 5 and the basis names that replay.

decisions.choice: Split exemption needs, per clause (cut on ';' and ','), a modal, no negation, no complaint word, and a move-verb-to-destination shape (Shape A, object words free of path-like tokens) or a part-subject 'be a follow-up job' shape (Shape B). A bare '<adjective> <noun>' with a modal never permits. A clause naming markers exempts only those parts.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 3 and 9: 'A wrong count could block the next job.' and 'This can stall multiple jobs.' must not switch the gate off, and a negation in another clause ('cannot wait; (3) may be a follow-up job') must not block a real permission.

risks.risk: The new check refuses more existing tests than the ones I read (the criterion 8 blast radius is wider than the files listed).

risks.risk: Stem overlap is a heuristic. A real reading may paraphrase a bullet without sharing an own stem and be refused, and dropping stems shared with siblings can leave a restated bullet with few own stems.
risks.mitigation: The cap of 2 shared stems, the stop list and the fall-back to all stems when an item has no own stems keep restating a few key words enough. Items with no stem are not checked. Table tests pin the Steward bullets in both directions and the silent-omission cases. The 5% share is an unmeasured estimate; the replay at verification measures the real figure and the producer updates the doc figure if its loop reports one.

risks.risk: The heuristic may refuse more than the hold limit (declared 5 plus 5 points = 10%) of past readings, since retries and Steward bullets are common.
risks.mitigation: The past or retry guard keeps retry readings that only recount a deferral. The doc comment says the figure is unmeasured and states the hold rule. If a replay in the producer's loop shows a higher share, the producer raises the declared figure with the measured basis rather than weakening the rule.

risks.risk: A deferral clause that mentions several parts could mark parts that are not deferred.
risks.mitigation: A deferral needs a phrase plus a marker or own-stem match in the same clause, with negation and past guards. Criteria are never searched. Unit tests pin 'Parts (1) and (2) now; part (3) is a follow-up job' (only (3) deferred) and a criterion that merely describes deferral.
